Rhapsodize

/RAP-suh-dyze/ - the stress falls on RAP · verb

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Rhapsodize means to engage in excessive enthusiasm.

Get Grandpa started on his old orchard and he will rhapsodize until the porch light comes on.

Worked Example

Our sommelier began to rhapsodize about the '09 vintage — comparing it to a cello, then to October, then to a small cathedral — while the soup went quietly cold.

To rhapsodize is to praise at length and altitude — talk that has left the ground and doesn't want to land. It is intransitive: you rhapsodize about or over something. The gusher enjoys it more than the listener, which is the word's gentle joke.

How Rhapsodize Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

gush

gush: a burst of over-eager praise — shorter-winded than rhapsodizing

rave: to praise wildly; critics rave in a sentence, rhapsodizers need an hour

Antonyms

understate

understate: to say deliberately less than you feel

grumble

grumble: low, unimpressed muttering

How Strong Is It? — mention → enthuse → rhapsodize

mention vs. rhapsodize

mention vs. rhapsodize: To mention a thing is to spend one sentence on it — the far, quiet end of this scale.

enthuse vs. rhapsodize

enthuse vs. rhapsodize: To enthuse is real, audible excitement, but rhapsodizing is stronger and longer than enthusing — praise settling in for the evening, with imagery.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — rhaps

Root — rhaps: to stitch, sew together (Greek rhaptein)

Root — od

Root — od: song (Greek ōidē)

Suffix — -ize

Suffix — -ize: verb ending: to do, to make

Put it together

Put it together: Rhaps- (to stitch) + od- (song) + -ize = to make stitched-together song. A Greek rhapsode recited epics — long poems 'stitched' from songs — and rhapsodize keeps the picture: enthusiasm so extended it turns into a recital. The song root stands alone in English as ode, a poem of praise.

Use the root in a new word: ode

Use the root in a new word: ode: For homework she wrote an ode to the school's vending machine, rhyming 'quarters' with 'headquarters.'

Root Check

Word Choice

playful / literary

Rhapsodize gently teases while it praises: it says the speaker's enthusiasm has become a performance. Use it for the friend who cannot stop describing the ramen. Gush is quicker and wetter; rave is louder; extol (in this unit's reference list) is the sober, formal cousin — you extol to persuade a committee, you rhapsodize because you can't help it.
